name: Special Interest
label: Rough Trade
lede: A Casio SK1 through cheap pedals, four transplants who had nothing to do with Katrina, and a New Orleans basement sound that ended up at No. 4 on Pitchfork's best albums of 2022.

eras.title: Four transplants and a Casio
eras.text: Special Interest started as a two-piece in New Orleans and grew into a four-piece of people who had all moved there for the queer, weird DIY scene. The sound began with one cheap keyboard and a lot of noise.

years.h: Two people in New Orleans become [[Special Interest|cb0a7ee8-69fe-409c-85ae-820e3f1e46d4]], a four-piece
years.p: [[Alli Logout|93a9c6b3-b38f-4f2a-a3d4-5c4ec51ebdb5]], [[Ruth Mascelli|50ef1d96-d3a1-4e7e-85ed-2dfaf4ce8fd4]], Maria Elena and Nathan Cassiani landed in the city from Texas, Pennsylvania and elsewhere, none of them there for Katrina.
years.xp:
NPR says the band formed in 2015 and started as a two-piece that grew; Wikipedia gives 2016. Mascelli, from Scranton, built the post-industrial foundation on a Casio SK1 run through cheap pedals and a noisy amp, NPR reports.

The members told NPR they were all transplants, and that the city's queer DIY scene was the draw. Logout told NME they came up on punk as a space for "everybody who was weird" before running into gatekeeping in bigger scenes.

years.src: Special Interest Bandcamp: Trust No Wave · Wikipedia: Special Interest
years.p: Eight tracks, four of them early versions of songs from Spiraling, plus a cover of Chrisma.
years.xp:
The band's Bandcamp dates the original demo to May 14, 2016. It came back as a vinyl reissue on Disciples in 2021, with a redesigned sleeve by Studio Tape Echo and an 8-page risographed zine, per Bandcamp and Wikipedia.

One of the demo tracks is titled "I'll Never Do Ketamine Again." Pitchfork called the reissue "a blistering vision of punk as possibility," as quoted on the band's Bandcamp page.

eras.title: Improvised in the studio
eras.text: Two albums in two years, both short on polish and long on anger. The second arrived in the middle of a pandemic and an uprising, with nowhere to tour it.

years.src: NPR · Gimmie Zine · Wikipedia: Special Interest
years.p: The debut came out on Raw Sugar Records in the US and Anxious Music in the UK.
years.xp:
NPR described it as fast, short and loud. Logout told Gimme that it was mostly improvised in the studio around her lyrics.

Sources spell the title both "Spiraling" (Wikipedia) and "Spiralling" (Bandcamp, NME).

q: Moving forward with love is what the album is all about.
years.src: SPIN · Gimmie Zine · Wikipedia: Special Interest
years.h: The Passion Of lands into the summer of 2020
years.p: Eleven tracks of industrial noise, dance beats and politics came out on Thrilling Living in the US and Night School in the UK, with no shows to play.
years.xp:
Spin reports the band debated the release date because it landed during the protests after the deaths of George Floyd and Breonna Taylor, then went ahead. The pandemic cancelled the album release shows and the touring.

Logout told Gimme it was her best work so far, and that she wrote the lyrics this time rather than improvising them on the day.

years.h: "Young, Gifted, Black, In Leather" is mostly improvised in the studio
years.p: The track ties leather in queer culture to leather in Black liberation movements.
years.xp: The Quietus reports the song was largely improvised in the studio. Logout told the same interview that if the band had to choose between playing with a band of people of color or a gay band, they would pick people of color.

eras.title: Across the Atlantic
eras.text: The British side of the story comes together: a demo reissue on a UK label, a single on another, and a signing to Rough Trade.

years.h: Signed to Rough Trade, with help from a taste for British bands
years.p: Wikipedia dates the signing to 2021, and Maria Elena told NME the band likes "a lot of British stuff."
years.xp: The group already had UK partners: Night School put out The Passion Of in Britain and Disciples reissued the 2016 demos. "Street Pulse Beat" came out the same year on Nude Club Records, with remixes including one by Boy Harsher.

eras.title: Endure
eras.text: The third album is the one that broke out: written in 2020 before a live audience could test it, made for dancing, and named one of the year's best by Pitchfork.

yt: Midnight Legend (feat. Mykki Blanco), official video
years.p: Logout directed the video and called the song a love song to everyone leaving the club at 6 AM.
years.xp: The Fader described the single as the polish of a Duran Duran hit with the post-punk atmosphere of Siouxsie and the Banshees. The announcement also carried a tour of North America and Europe running from September to December 2022, from San Diego to London to New Orleans.

years.h: Endure: written in 2020, finished for the dance floor
years.p: Recorded at HighTower in New Orleans with engineer James Whitten, it swaps chaos for playful, danceable songs and closes with the eight-minute "LA Blues."
years.xp:
Writing began in the summer of 2020 in a large practice space that allowed distancing. Spin reports it was the first Special Interest album written entirely before any live testing, with more overdubs and deliberate production than before. Wikipedia lists the recording period as 2020 to 2022, with the band itself as producer.

Logout described two halves to the record: personal growth, and everything going on outside that you can't change.

years.src: Wikipedia: Endure · Album of the Year
years.h: Pitchfork: Best New Music, and No. 4 of the year
years.p: Sasha Geffen reviewed it; Pitchfork later ranked it No. 4 on its 50 Best Albums of 2022.
years.xp:
Geffen wrote that the band "pushes their sound to both its bleakest and its sweetest brinks." Wikipedia lists the 8.8 and the Best New Music tag, and Album of the Year lists the review as 88.

Metacritic has it at 84. The Guardian gave four stars, Loud and Quiet 9/10, and Album of the Year shows it at No. 2 on SPIN's 2022 list and No. 6 at No Ripcord.

years.h: "(Herman's) House" turns to the Angola Three
years.p: The video and song deal with the imprisonment of the Angola Three, per SPIN.
years.xp: The same SPIN interview notes "Concerning Peace" documents the political turmoil of June 2020.

eras.title: Scattered, still touring
eras.text: The band is no longer all in one city, but the record keeps them on the road.

years.p: The single came out in 2023, alongside a remix album, Endure (Remixed).
years.xp: By February 2023, NME reported that Logout had moved to Los Angeles and Elena to Oakland, while Mascelli and Cassiani stayed in New Orleans.
